svg.title: 3. Tenant isolation and east-west traffic
svg.text: Hard tenancy goes in its own cluster and account
Tenant isolation inside the shared cluster, and service-to-service calls across clusters and accounts with VPC Lattice
fit on the tainted search pool.
Guardrails every namespace gets from the tenant manifest
Isolation: default-deny NetworkPolicy (VPC CNI network policy agent), PSA "restricted",
Kyverno: no hostPath, no privileged, images only from our ECR, PDB requires 2+ replicas
Fairness: ResourceQuota, LimitRange defaults, PriorityClass per tier, dedicated NodePools
Identity: access entries per team, Pod Identity per service account, no node role sharing
Soft tenancy (namespaces) is fine for teams that trust each other
and share a release process. It is not a security boundary
against a hostile workload: the kernel, the nodes and the API
So a separate cluster in a separate account for:
- PCI scope (payments), regulated data, customer-supplied code
- workloads that need cluster-wide admin or their own CRDs
- anything whose blast radius you would not share
VPC Lattice then joins them back together at the service level,
without peering VPCs or sharing nodes.
AWS Gateway API Controller turns the
HTTPRoute into a Lattice service and a
Node security group allows inbound from the
VPC Lattice managed prefix list only.
No VPC peering, no Transit Gateway route
Same CIDR as the platform VPC, so peering and
Transit Gateway are off the table. Lattice does not
route between VPCs, it proxies requests, so the
overlap does not matter. invoice calls catalog;
SigV4-signed with its Pod Identity creds
3 auth policy checks the IAM principal
4 Lattice forwards to payments pod IPs
